Manage and refer urgently:
If septic arthritis, injury/fracture, suspected secondary gout (haematological malignancy) or known gout with chronic kidney disease, refer.
JOINT SYMPTOMS

Approach to the patient with a joint symptom/s not needing urgent attention • Check joints and ask patient to place hands behind head, then behind back. Bury nails in palm to make a fist and open hand. Press palms together with elbows lifted. Walk. Sit and stand up with arms folded. • Is there any of: joint warm/tender/swollen or unable to do all actions comfortably?

Sprain/strain likely • Rest and elevate joint. • Apply ice and a pressure bandage. • Give paracetamol 500mg-1g 4-6 hourly (up to 4g in 24 hours) as needed for up to 5 days. If no response, give ibuprofen 400mg 8 hourly with/ after food as needed for up to 7 days (avoid if peptic ulcer, asthma, hypertension, heart failure, kidney disease, pregnant). • If available, arrange physiotherapy. • Advise to mobilise joint after 2-3 days, if not too painful. • Review after 1 week: if no better, arrange x-ray and doctor review.

• Give paracetamol 500mg-1g 4-6 hourly (up to 4g in 24 hours) as needed for up to 5 days and methyl salicylate ointment to rub on affected joint. If no response, give ibuprofen 400mg 8 hourly with/ after food as needed for up to 5 days (avoid if peptic ulcer, asthma, hypertension, heart failure, kidney disease, pregnant). • Test for HIV 124. • Review after 1 month or sooner if joint pain worsens. If worsens, refer. • While waiting for appointment: - If pain in hands or feet, refer to occupational therapist, if available. - If pain in other joints, refer to physiotherapist, if available. - Assess and advise on chronic pain 76.
